translation: Arjuna said: I long to thoroughly comprehend the ultimate essence and core definition of formal renunciation (Sannyasa), as well as the nature of relinquishment (Tyaga), in their distinct, separate jurisdictions, O mighty-armed Lord of the senses, O destroyer of the demon Keshi!

The Blessed Lord said: The ancient seers understand the complete abdication of reward- driven, desire-fueled actions (kamyanam karmanam) to be formal renunciation (Sannyasa). While the highly learned experts define the absolute surrender of the personal rewards of all daily obligations to be relinquishment (Tyaga).

Some analytical philosophers declare that all forms of material action are inherently packed with friction and flaws, and therefore must be completely cast off like a defect. While other sages vigorously maintain that actions of social sacrifice, charity, and self-discipline must never be abandoned under any circumstance.

Listen now to My definitive, unshakeable verdict regarding this matter of relinquishment, O best of the Bharata dynasty! For relinquishment, O tiger among men, has been systematically shown to be of three distinct types across cosmic science.

Actions of social sacrifice, charity, and self-discipline must absolutely never be abandoned; they must be executed as mandatory duties. For sacrifice, charity, and self-discipline act as the vital, essential purifiers of human intelligence (pavanani manishinam).
simple_explanation: Krishna blocks the exit door for lazy escapists. You cannot drop your social actions under the protective excuse of "spirituality." If you stop running your public hospitals, distributing resources, or maintaining physical discipline, you are not ascending—you are simply causing social collapse. Action is the engine that filters away individual selfishness.

translation: But let it be understood that even these essential duties must be executed completely casting off personal attachment and dropping all anxious desire for individual prizes, O Partha! Such is My definitive, absolute, and supreme verdict.

The complete renunciation or desertion of a prescribed, mandatory obligation (niyatasya karmanah) is entirely improper and invalid. Fleeing from it out of a temporary state of deluded confusion is branded as Tamasa relinquishment.

He who abandons a necessary duty simply because it appears unpleasant, shouting "this work brings heavy physical hardship and pain!" executes nothing but a passion-driven Rajasa relinquishment. He completely fails to harvest the spiritual credit born of real renunciation.

When a mandatory, prescribed obligation is executed single-mindedly because it is an objective necessity that ought to be done, O Arjuna, thoroughly casting off personal attachment and dropping all longing for rewards—that relinquishment is evaluated by Me as Sattvikah.

The genuine practitioner of relinquishment, thoroughly saturated with pure goodness (sattva- samavishto), possessed of razor-sharp intelligence (medhavi), his inner doubts completely slashed to pieces, neither avoids an unpleasant, grueling task nor develops a clinging attachment to an enjoyable one.

For it is physically impossible for any embodied human being (dehabhrita) to completely cease from all physical actions without exception. Therefore, he alone who effectively renounces the personal rewards of his action is definitively designated by the title of a true practitioner of relinquishment (Tyagi).

Unpleasant, pleasant, and multi-mixed—this is the threefold binding consequence of karma that accrues after death onto those who have failed to practice detachment (atyaginam). But absolutely no binding outcome ever touches those who operate in a state of genuine, detached renunciation.

Learn now from Me, O mighty-armed warrior, these five mandatory operational variables (karanani) outlined in the definitive conclusions of the Sankhya science for the successful execution of every single action in the universe.
simple_explanation: Krishna introduces a comprehensive analytical model of action, dismantling the dangerous, lazy superstition of fatalism. Success in the physical world is not driven by some magical, arbitrary decree of luck. It is the mathematical outcome of these five specific variables operating in unison. If your project fails, analyze these components scientifically instead of crying over "destiny."

translation: The physical arena or locus of action (Adhishthanam), the individualized agent (Karta), the distinct varieties of biological instruments and tools utilized (Karanam), the multi-layered distinct exertions and operations deployed (Chesta), and matching these four, the unmanifest cosmic law of causation acting as the fifth variable (Daivam).

Whatever action a human being initiates using his physical body, his vocal speech, or his internal thoughts—whether it is perfectly aligned with objective justice (nyayyam) or completely contrary to it—these five variables serve as its direct, producing causes.

This being the absolute structural reality, he who out of an unrefined, uneducated intellect views his isolated, absolute Self as the sole independent author of action—that short-sighted fool is completely blind to the laws of nature.

He whose core heart is entirely free from the illusion of egoistic agency (nahankrito bhavo), and whose analytical intellect is never stained or clouded by personal malice—even if he neutralizes these hostile aggregations in battle, he does not kill, nor is he ever shackled by the consequences of his action.

Theoretical knowledge (Jnanam), the object to be known (Jneyam), and the knowing consciousness (Parijnata)—these three constitute the internal, threefold impulse that sparks action (karma-chodana). While the instrument (Karanam), the action itself (Karma), and the agent (Karta) form the threefold physical execution of action (karma-sangrahah).

In the definitive taxonomy of the science of nature's properties (Guna-sankhyane), theoretical knowledge, the action, and the agent are also declared to be of three distinct types according to their internal qualities. Listen carefully to My structural breakdown of these variables.

That knowledge by which a observer directly perceives a single, imperishable, undivided Reality (ekam bhavam-avyayam) as running continuously across all the distinct, multi- divided living entities of the world—know that unified vision to belong to the mode of pure goodness (Satvikam).

But that knowledge which looks out at creation exclusively through the lens of fragmentation, viewing all living creatures as separate, isolated, and fundamentally disconnected entities locked in perpetual conflict—know that short-sighted vision to belong to the mode of Rajas.

And that narrow, stultifying view which pathologically clutches onto a single, isolated, tiny variable as if it constituted the complete whole (kritsna-vat), which is irrational (ahaitukam), completely detached from objective reality, and wretchedly petty—that blind vision is classified as Tamasam.
simple_explanation: Krishna provides a razor-sharp critique of religious and political fanaticism (Tamasi Jnana). When an unthinking crowd latches onto a single superficial symbol or localized identity, ignoring the vast architecture of truth, and proclaims that "this tiny point is everything that matters," they are operating in absolute Tamas. True wisdom expands and unifies; ignorance narrows down and destroys.

translation: That action which is executed in strict accordance with mandatory regulations, free from emotional attachment, performed entirely without attraction or aversion (araga-dveshatah), by an individual completely free from the hunger for personal rewards—that labor is designated as Sattvikam.

But that action which is executed by an individual driven by burning material ambition, or orchestrated to satisfy personal pride and egotism, involving immense, crushing, and stressful strain (bahulayasam)—that labor is classified as Rajasam.

That action which is initiated out of blind, unthinking delusion, with absolute disregard for long-term consequences (anubandham), economic depletion, environmental injury (hinsam), or one's own real internal capacity (paurusham)—that chaotic labor is designated as Tamasam.

The agent who is free from personal attachment, free from egotistical self-glorification (naham-vadi), overflowing with unswerving fortitude and resilient enthusiasm (dhriti-utsaha- samanvitah), and remains completely unmoved and stable under success or sudden failure— that worker is designated as Sattvikah.

The agent who is deeply attached, restlessly hunting after personal rewards, greedy, predatory and violent by nature (hinsatmakah), impure in conduct, and continuously tossed around by waves of wild exultation or stinging grief—that worker is branded as Rajasah.

The agent who is undisciplined, crude and uneducated, stubborn, deceitful (shatho), malicious, chronically lazy, drowning in perpetual self-pity and depression (vishadi), and wasting time in chronic procrastination (dirgha-sutri)—that worker is designated as Tamasah.

Listen now to My complete, exhaustive classification of the analytical intellect (Buddhi) and fortitude (Dhriti), divided into three distinct types according to the modes of nature, detailed for you with succinct clarity, O Dhananjaya!

That intellect which knows exactly when to step forward into action (pravrittim) and when to step back in restraint (nivrattim); which accurately identifies what fit to be done (karya) and what is unfit (akarya); which comprehends what is truly dangerous (bhaya) and what is safe (abhaya); and understands what leads to mental bondage and what unlocks ultimate liberation—that intellect is Sattviki, O Partha!

That intellect by which a person misinterprets and holds a distorted view regarding righteousness (Dharma) and lawlessness (Adharma), and cannot clearly distinguish what fit to be done from what is unfit, O Partha, is classified as Rajasi.

That intellect which, completely enveloped by the dense fog of mental darkness, stands reality on its head, evaluating lawlessness (Adharma) to be true righteousness, and perceives every single value across life in a totally topsy-turvy, inverted manner—that intellect is Tamasi, O Partha!

That unswerving willpower and fortitude (Dhriti) by which a practitioner firmly stabilizes, regulates, and coordinates the operations of his thoughts, his vital life-currents (Prana), and his sensory organs through focused Yoga—that fortitude is Sattviki, O Partha!

But that willpower by which a person stubbornly clings onto traditional rituals (Dharma), material luxuries (Kama), and financial assets (Artha), driven by obsession and a permanent craving for personal rewards, O Arjuna, is classified as Rajasi.

That stubborn rigidity by which a dull-witted fool refuse to let go of excessive sleep (svapnam), constant fear, grief, chronic depression, and arrogant pride—that toxic willpower is Tamasi, O Partha!

Listen now to My systematic analysis of the three distinct types of happiness (Sukham), O foremost of the Bharata dynasty! That happiness in which a human being learns to find deep delight through consistent internal training (abhyasat), and by which he successfully terminates all his worldly miseries;

Which feels like bitter poison at the initial start (agre visham-iva) because it demands intense discipline and shattering labor, but tastes like the nectar of immortality in its final transformation (pariname amritopamam)—that happiness is declared to be Sattvikam, born of the serene tranquility of an intellect anchored in the Self.

That pleasure which surges up from the sudden contact of the physical senses with their corresponding objects, which tastes like sweet nectar at the initial start, but transforms into toxic poison at the final outcome (pariname visham-iva)—that pleasure is recorded as Rajasam.
simple_explanation: This model maps the structural economics of human happiness. Rajasi pleasure is an unbacked loan: it gives an immediate burst of sensory delight, but charges crushing interest in the form of disease, addiction, or fractured relationships later. Sattviki happiness is an investment: it demands the hardship of study and discipline first, but pays out permanent dividends of mental peace and stability at the end.

translation: That superficial pleasure which both at its start and throughout its continuity serves only to blind and stupefy the Self, originating directly from excessive sleep, chronic laziness, and reckless confusion—that dark stagnation is classified as Tamasam.

There is absolutely no entity or creature to be found anywhere, whether down here across the planet earth or up among the cosmic forces in heavenly planes, which is free from the structural grip of these three modes born of material nature.

The social classifications and fields of duty belonging to the scholars (Brahmans), the administrators and warriors (Kshatriyas), the merchants and agriculturalists (Vaishyas), and the laborers (Shudras), O scorcher of foes, are systematically allocated based on their internal talents, active capabilities, and nature's qualities (svabhava-prabhavair-gunaih).
simple_explanation: Sri Krishna thoroughly shatters the corrupt, medieval interpretation of the caste system as a rigid hereditary birthright. The text explicitly patterns classification upon Guna and Karma (qualities and active labor), not upon parental bloodlines. If a person born into a scholar's family exhibits laziness and deceit (Tamas), he belongs to the under-class. If a person born into a laborer's home exhibits high statesmanship and military genius (Rajas-Sattva), he is functionally a Kshatriya.

translation: Tranquility of mind, strict mastery over the senses, self-discipline, internal and external cleanliness, patient forgiveness, straight integrity, scriptural knowledge, direct verified realization, and unswerving conviction in cosmic order—this constitutes the natural, built-in duty of the intellectual class (Brahma-karma).

Heroic valor, radiant majesty, iron fortitude, supreme skill and efficiency in administration (dakshyam), refusing to turn your back or flee during a battle, generous philanthropy, and majestic command statesmanship—this constitutes the natural, built-in duty of the warrior- ruler class (Kshatra-karma).

Agriculture, cow protection, and commercial trade constitute the natural field of labor for the merchant class (Vaishya-karma). While manual service, mechanical support, and assistance represent the natural field of duty for the working class (Shudra-karma).

By remaining intensely focused on the execution of his own designated field of duty (sve sve karmani bhirataho), a human being secures absolute spiritual perfection. Listen now to the exact method by which a worker anchored in his specific labor captures this perfection.

From whom all living creatures emerge into history, and by whose unmanifest presence this entire universe is pervaded—by transforming his daily, assigned professional labor into an act of worship (svakarmana tam-abhyarchya) dedicated to that Source, a human being secures absolute perfection.
simple_explanation: This is the ultimate sanctification of daily human labor. You do not need to abandon your welding tools, your ledger books, or your military weapons to find God. When a street sweeper clears a road efficiently to prevent disease, or when an engineer builds a flawless bridge to protect a population, their professional excellence is a grander sacrificial offering than pouring tons of clarified butter into material fires. Labor is a form of prayer.

translation: One's own assigned lane of duty (Svadharma), though executed with visible imperfections, is far superior to the highly polished track of another's duty (Paradharma). Executing that labor which matches your own natural, biological talent (svabhava-niyatam), you can never incur sin.

One should never abandon that professional labor which emerges naturally from his innate talent (sahajam karma), O son of Kunti, even if it appears packed with apparent strains or defects! For every single human undertaking in this material world is wrapped inside some friction, exactly like a bright fire is naturally accompanied by a column of dark smoke.

He whose analytical intellect is entirely unattached under all circumstances, who has subdued his lower self, from whom all material cravings have departed, ascends by the path of internal renunciation to the supreme apex of actionless freedom (naishkarmya-siddhim).

Having successfully won that professional perfection, how he seamlessly merges into the Absolute Brahman, which represents the supreme apex of realized wisdom—listen now to My succinct, summary explanation, O son of Kunti.

Endowed with a completely purified, razor-sharp intellect, tightly anchoring the self through unswerving willpower, completely cutting off sound and all other objective sensory inputs, and entirely casting out attraction and aversion;

Retiring periodically to quiet, undisturbed locations, eating lightly and healthily, with vocal expression, physical body, and thoughts brought under complete control, permanently absorbed in deep meditation (Dhyana-yoga), and taking firm shelter within systematic detachment;

Thoroughly shedding raw egotism, brute force, arrogance, lust, rage, and the urge for possessiveness—free from the illusion of ownership (nirmamah) and completely pacified, he becomes fully qualified to achieve absolute union with Brahman.

Established in union with the Divine (Brahma-bhutah), his core heart overflowing with profound serenity, he neither grieves over past events nor craves future circumstances. Looking upon all living creatures with a completely equal, impartial eye, he wins My supreme devotion.

Through this supreme devotion, he acquires accurate, direct knowledge of My universal reality—comprehending who I am and what My limitless nature is in its true essence. Knowing Me in truth, he swiftly enters straight into My supreme being.

Even while remaining heavily engaged in the execution of all types of material and professional labor day after day, by taking absolute refuge in Me, he successfully secures by My grace that ancient, everlasting, and imperishable State.

Mentally surrendering all your actions unto My cosmic law, looking upon Me as your supreme refuge, taking firm shelter within the Yoga of clear discernment (Buddhi-yogam), keep your consciousness focused on My presence at all moments.

With your mind saturated by My presence, you will easily cross over all the impossible gridlocks and dangers (sarva-durgani) of life by My grace. But if you refuse to listen, driven by raw egotism and pride (ahankarat), you will be utterly ruined and lost.

If, taking stubborn refuge within raw egoism, you formulate this thought: "I will not fight this battle!" your steel resolve is entirely vain and hollow. For your inherent Kshatriya nature and biological wiring will eventually wake up and drag you back onto the field by force.

Shackled tightly by the momentum of your own natural attributes and past character conditioning, O son of Kunti, that very duty which you currently refuse to execute due to a temporary state of delusion, you will be forced to execute helplessly anyway later under worse terms.

The absolute Sovereign Lord (Ishvarah) resides permanently seated within the heart core of every single living creature, O Arjuna! Operating through His cosmic laws, He coordinates and rotates all created beings who are mounted like passengers upon this material machinery (yantra-rudhani) formed of nature.

Take absolute refuge in Him alone with your entire being, O descendant of Bharata! By His supreme grace, you will obtain absolute inner peace (Param Shantim) and achieve that ancient, everlasting Abode.

Thus has this profound wisdom, which is subtler and more secret than secrecy itself, been fully detailed to you by Me. Reflected upon this exhaustive science in its entirety (vimrishyaitad-asheshena), and then act according to your own free choice!
simple_explanation: This verse highlights the supreme, magnificent respect for human free will built into Vedic philosophy. Sri Krishna does not use emotional brainwashing, moral threats, or military coercion to force Arjuna to move. He presents a comprehensive layout of the cosmos, details the mechanics of duty and psychological wiring, and then steps back, telling the warrior: "Think it through independently, and make your own mature choice."

translation: Listen once more to My absolute final, most profound word, which is the secret of all secrets! Because you are deeply dear to Me and stand as My unswerving companion, I unfold this ultimate instruction for your highest welfare.

Saturate your mind with My presence; become My dedicated worker; offer all your sacrifices to My global mission; bow down before My universal presence. Doing so, you will ascend straight into My reality; I give you My unassailable, true pledge, because you are deeply dear to Me.

Thoroughly relinquishing all localized, relative moral structures and dependencies (sarva- dharman parityajya), take absolute refuge in Me alone as the single, underlying Axis of existence. I shall completely liberate you from the binding consequences of all errors and sins; shake off your anxiety!
simple_explanation: This represents the ultimate verse of complete spiritual surrender (Charama Shloka). Sarva- dharman does not mean abandoning ethics or sliding into lawlessness. In Vedic grammar, it means rising above limited, emotional, or conditional loyalties (such as Arjuna’s distorted attachment to family bloodlines, which he mistakenly called his "Kula Dharma" in Chapter 1). When relative social ethics clash with global justice, drop the narrow, localized loyalty and align yourself exclusively with the Supreme Cosmic Law.

translation: This profound science must absolutely never be communicated to one who is devoid of self- discipline (natapaskaya), nor to one who lacks dedication, nor to a listener who displays no desire to learn, nor to someone who maliciously mocks My universal presence.

He who teaches and propagates this supreme, profound science among My dedicated workers, executing the highest service to Me, will undoubtedly ascend straight into My reality; there is absolutely no shadow of doubt about this.

Absolutely no one exists among all human beings across the globe who executes a grander, more precious service to My mission than he! Nor will there ever be anyone else in the future of history who is dearer to Me on earth than him.

And he who regularly studies, reflects upon, and absorbs this deeply righteous dialogue of ours (dharmyam samvadam-avayoho), offers onto Me the majestic sacrifice of knowledge (Jnana-yajna)—such is My definitive, unshakeable verdict.
